title: FIDES Topic Content File
description: Schema for a single topics/<slug>.json content file in the FIDES catechism-database. Every question must carry at least one authoritative Magisterial citation (CCC, Scripture, Council text, or magisterial document) -- Church Fathers alone are never sufficient.

topic.description: Must match this file's top-level 'topic' field.

level.description: Topics no longer share one fixed level count -- see the Aug 13, 2026 curriculum-design debate. This schema-level max is a loose outer bound (the highest ceiling any topic reaches); each topic's real ceiling is enforced by its own TopicMaster.levelNames.count in the app, not here.

difficultyElo.description: Seed Elo difficulty for this question, consumed by EloEngine.

correctAnswer.description: Used by multiple_choice (string, must match a choice), true_false (boolean), and fill_blank (string). Omitted for matching_pairs, where 'pairs' itself is the answer key.

explanation.description: Shown after answering; must stand on its own as a short catechetical note.

hint.description: Optional. Shown by the in-app guide mascot if the user pauses too long before answering. Falls back to a generic line when absent.

citations.description: Must contain at least one citation whose type is ccc, scripture, council, magisterial_document, or catechism. A church_father citation may supplement these but can never stand alone.

audit_status.description: Set to 'audited' only once a credentialed theological reviewer has actually approved this specific question -- see sign_audit_manifest.swift, which reads exactly this field to build manifest.json's signed auditedQuestionIDs list. Omit entirely for unreviewed content; the app and this field both default to 'pending' when absent. Setting this by hand does NOT itself unlock anything in the app -- AuditManifestVerifier only trusts IDs that are also present in manifest.json's cryptographically signed auditedQuestionIDs list, precisely so a stray edit here (or a compromised GitHub account) can't forge an audited claim.

contributors.description: GitHub handles of contributors, shown on the in-app credits screen. Optional; omitted entirely for most content so far.

miniGameEligible.description: True only for a question cleared for mini-game use -- either a claim unambiguous enough for a timed binary sort (multiple_choice/true_false; feeds 'Heresy or Orthodox' and 'Virtue or Vice'; e.g. 'Arianism denies Christ's divinity' -- clearly true or false, not a live theological nuance), a matching_pairs question (feeds the untimed 'Saint / Feast-Day', 'Church Latin Match', and 'Prayer Match' games, which don't carry the same binary-format risk), or a fill_blank question testing recall of a known text (feeds the untimed 'Prayer Fill-In' game, added Sep 1, 2026). See MINI-GAMES-SPEC.md's content-type taxonomy. Defaults to false when absent, so every existing question is safe-by-default and nothing becomes mini-game content without this explicit, reviewed tag. validate.py rejects true on any type other than multiple_choice/true_false/matching_pairs/fill_blank, and on level 6+ of the six hard-gated topics specifically (levels 1-5 of those topics already shipped at launch and are fine).

reference.description: e.g. 'CCC 881', 'Matthew 16:18-19', 'First Council of Nicaea (325)', 'Pius IX, Ineffabilis Deus (1854)', 'St. Augustine of Hippo'

note.description: Optional short clarifying note about the citation.

quote.description: Optional excerpt of the actual source text this citation points to -- a short, specific passage (e.g. the one sentence of CCC 253 that's relevant), not the full paragraph or chapter. Added Aug 12, 2026; most existing citations don't have one yet.
